photon.short: A single packet of light. Its energy is set by its colour: bluer light comes in bigger packets.

band-gap.short: The minimum energy an electron in a semiconductor must gain to break free and carry current. Silicon's is about 1.12 eV.

semiconductor.short: A material, such as silicon, that conducts electricity much better than an insulator but much worse than a metal, and whose conductivity can be tuned.

electronvolt.short: The energy one electron gains crossing one volt: 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ joules. Handy for photons: visible light carries 1.6 to 3.3 eV.

irradiance.short: Sunlight power arriving per square metre, in watts per square metre (W/m²). Bright midday sun is about 1000 W/m².

peak-sun-hours.short: A day's sunlight energy expressed as hours of 1000 W/m² sunshine. 5 kWh/m² in a day is 5 peak sun hours.

capacity-factor.short: Energy a plant actually produces in a year divided by what it would produce running flat out all year.

lcoe.short: The average price per unit of energy a plant must earn over its life to pay back its building, running and financing costs.
